entertainment-notes.ticketNote: Show listings and advertised prices were checked November 6. Use the official ticket links for current availability.
entertainment-notes.travelNote: Walk and ride times are estimates from The Driskill, not live route calculations.

festival.name: Out of Bounds Comedy Festival
festival.description: The festival supplies this Saturday’s special programming at Fallout, ColdTowne and Dougherty. Bills can mix improv, sketch, clowning and music; the formats below help you choose.
festival.bookingAdvice: For one or two shows, buy individual tickets. General admission is $22.35 including fees per block; eligible students, seniors and active military pay $17.10 including fees. An all-access badge is $129 and still requires show reservations.
festival.availabilityNote: Several recommended blocks offered tickets when checked November 6. Availability can change; each block has its own ticket page.

hideout.name: The Hideout Theatre
hideout.address: 5555 N Lamar Blvd, Suite B103, Austin, TX 78751
hideout.status: The Hideout has moved to North Lamar. No public show for Saturday, November 7 was confirmed on its current calendar when checked, so it is not listed as a Saturday option.
hideout.tip: Use the new North Lamar address if visiting; the old Congress Avenue location is no longer the destination.

hotelMusic.name: The Victorian
hotelMusic.status: The venue advertises Thursday–Saturday music from 9pm to midnight, but no named November 7 act was confirmed. Treat it as a convenient possibility to check with the hotel rather than a dated show recommendation.

entertainment.name: Soul Man Sam at Antone’s
entertainment.description: A strong choice for a classic Austin music evening without a car. Soul Man Sam brings blues and soul to Antone’s, a short walk from the hotel. Plan on a lively club show: general admission is mainly standing, with only limited seating available on a first-come basis.
entertainment.price: Artist lists $15 cover; online fees may apply
entertainment.tip: Have dinner downtown, then arrive closer to doors if a seat matters. A ticket does not reserve seating.

entertainment.name: Kris Kimura Quartet at Parker
entertainment.kicker: Reserved seats and American Songbook jazz
entertainment.description: Kris Kimura joins the Ryan Davis Trio for vocals, woodwinds and familiar jazz standards. This intimate listening room is the best fit for a group that wants to sit comfortably and focus on the performance. Choose the early show for an easier evening or the later set after dinner.
entertainment.price: Check ticket page for current seat prices
entertainment.tip: Choose seats together when booking. The room is geared toward listening, so save extended conversation for before or after the set.

entertainment.name: Tommy Howard Quintet at Elephant Room
entertainment.description: Head downstairs on Congress Avenue for a small, atmospheric jazz room with an informal bar feel. Tommy Howard’s quintet plays Saturday at 9pm. It is an appealing option when the group would rather pay a modest cover at the door than choose a reserved-seat show in advance.
entertainment.tip: Arrive around opening if you want the best chance of seats together. Reservations are not available.

entertainment.name: Kabaka Pyramid & Bebble Rockers
entertainment.description: A more energetic late-night option on East Sixth: Kabaka Pyramid blends reggae, hip-hop and dancehall with his band, the Bebble Rockers. Ras I-Dre and the Royal Frequency open, with DJ Mista B also on the bill. Choose this for dancing and a full club night rather than an early finish.
entertainment.price: $35 advance / $45 day of show, plus any fees
entertainment.tip: The advertised 9pm time is doors, not a confirmed Kabaka Pyramid start time.

entertainment.name: The Peterson Brothers at Continental Club
entertainment.kicker: Blues, soul and funk on South Congress
entertainment.description: The Peterson Brothers mix blues, soul, funk and jazz at one of South Congress’s longstanding music clubs. The relatively early set makes this easy to pair with a South Congress stroll and dinner. It is a worthwhile short ride if the group wants to see a different part of Austin.
entertainment.price: Check ticket page for current price
entertainment.tip: Plan around this particular set; the club may have a separate event later in the evening.

entertainment.name: Dale Watson at Broken Spoke
entertainment.description: Make this the evening’s destination if country music and dancing appeal. Dale Watson plays the Broken Spoke dancehall at 9pm, and the earlier two-step lesson offers a way to join in even without much experience. The atmosphere and location make this more of an outing than a quick downtown stop.
entertainment.price: Lesson $10 + cover; check venue for Saturday cover
entertainment.tip: The dancehall opens at 7:15pm. The venue asks lesson participants to arrive by 7:30pm to sign up for the 8pm class.

entertainment.name: An afternoon or early evening at Saxon Pub
entertainment.kicker: Free afternoon music or Courtney Patton at 6
entertainment.description: Saxon Pub offers a useful daytime music option: Suburban Beat plays a free afternoon set. Return or stay in the neighborhood for Courtney Patton’s early evening show, with country and Americana songwriting. These are separate performances, so the free afternoon listing does not include admission to the later show.
entertainment.price: Afternoon free, tips appreciated · Courtney $25 advance
entertainment.bestFor: Hearing music without staying out late
entertainment.tip: Courtney Patton’s show is 21+. Advance admission gets you in but does not guarantee a seat.

entertainment.name: Out of Bounds at Fallout Theater
entertainment.kicker: The easiest festival show to reach on foot
entertainment.description: This 6pm festival bill combines Booze & The Boys, Comedy Fusion, and Touch Baseball with guest Oscar Montoya. Expect a mix of theatrical improv, stand-up meeting improv, and a character-driven scene. Fallout is the most convenient Out of Bounds venue from the hotel, leaving the rest of the evening open.
entertainment.bestFor: A convenient first taste of the festival
entertainment.tip: Buy the individual show ticket if this is your only festival stop. Discount tickets for students, seniors and active military are $17.10 including fees.
details: Fallout also hosts festival bills at 8pm and 10pm; see the full Saturday schedule below.

entertainment.name: Musical comedy at ColdTowne Cabaret
entertainment.kicker: Out of Bounds: songs, a blind date and a musical
entertainment.description: For a varied, music-friendly comedy evening, this Cabaret bill pairs Lizzie Kaniecki’s comedy songs with Meet Cute, where a real blind date inspires improv, and Kyle & Kendon: The Musical. The last act creates a musical on the spot. ColdTowne’s Main Stage and Cabaret share the same East Austin address.
entertainment.bestFor: A group that enjoys musical comedy
entertainment.tip: Choose the Cabaret 8pm listing when booking; the Main Stage has a different show at the same time.
details: The Cabaret’s 6pm bill is another good variety pick: But of Mind, Wickey and Ivories Guy, with improv ranging from a Twilight Zone-style story to music.

entertainment.name: Out of Bounds at Dougherty Arts Center
entertainment.kicker: Three improv groups in an early festival slot
entertainment.description: Y’All We Asian, Gooses and The Knuckleball Now! share this 6pm bill at Dougherty Arts Center. It is a straightforward choice for a group specifically interested in improv, with three different teams in one festival block. The venue is south of the river, so allow time for the ride from downtown.
entertainment.bestFor: An early show devoted to improv
entertainment.tip: Terry Black’s is nearby on Barton Springs Road, but leave a generous buffer if combining barbecue with a fixed showtime.
details: Dougherty also has festival blocks at 8pm and 10pm. The 8pm bill includes Drunk Theatre and is a rowdier adult choice.

entertainment.name: Esther’s Follies
entertainment.kicker: Sketches, political satire, music and magic
entertainment.description: A long-running Austin variety show with topical sketches, musical numbers and stage magic, just a few blocks along Sixth Street. This is a useful choice when the group wants a polished comedy show with several kinds of entertainment in one sitting. The format is scripted variety rather than an improv bill.
entertainment.tip: Reserve the specific Saturday performance you want. Expect political satire and adult humor.

entertainment.name: ComedySportz in Round Rock
entertainment.description: Teams compete in improv games shaped by audience suggestions, making this the clearest all-ages comedy option in the list. It is held at Premier Music Academy in Round Rock, well outside the downtown walking area. Choose it if clean, family-friendly improv matters enough to justify the longer drive.
entertainment.address: 1400 E Old Settlers Blvd, Suite 116, Round Rock, TX 78664
entertainment.price: Listed at $15; check any ticketing fees
entertainment.bestFor: Clean improv for a mixed-age group
entertainment.tip: Budget for the return ride as well as the ticket. This is in Round Rock, not central Austin.

explore-bars.name: The Driskill's historic interiors
explore-bars.description: The hotel itself is a worthwhile first stop. Opened in 1886 by cattle baron Jesse Driskill, it has hosted generations of Texas political and cultural life. Take a few unhurried minutes with the lobby, historic details and public gathering spaces before heading out into the city.
explore-bars.hours: A flexible stop before or after the day's outings
explore-bars.price: Free to explore the hotel's public areas
explore-bars.bestFor: A short introduction to old Austin
explore-bars.tip: Ask the concierge about the building's stories and any guided history offerings during your stay.

explore-bars.name: Texas Capitol & grounds
explore-bars.description: Walk north toward the Capitol for architecture, Texas history and a good sense of the city's geography. The free guided tour is an easy way to get more from the visit, with guides explaining the building and legislature. Leave time to wander the landscaped grounds and look back down Congress Avenue.
explore-bars.bestFor: History, architecture and an easy morning outing
explore-bars.tip: Tours generally leave every 15–30 minutes, last about 40 minutes and start inside the South Foyer. Small groups can join without arranging a large-group visit.

sources.label: Texas State Preservation Board: hours and address

explore-bars.name: Bullock Texas State History Museum
explore-bars.description: An appealing follow-on to the Capitol, with three floors devoted to Texas history. The remains of the seventeenth-century French ship La Belle are a standout. This is a good choice when the family wants a substantial indoor activity; allow a couple of hours rather than trying to squeeze it into a quick stop.
explore-bars.price: Adult museum admission $22; films are separate
explore-bars.bestFor: Texas history and an afternoon indoors
explore-bars.tip: Pair it with the Capitol or nearby Blanton. Choose one museum for a relaxed visit; doing both makes a much fuller day.

explore-bars.name: Blanton Museum of Art
explore-bars.kicker: Art, color and a quiet pause
explore-bars.description: The art-focused alternative to the Bullock, at the south edge of the UT campus. Its special draw is Ellsworth Kelly's Austin, a building conceived as an artwork, with luminous colored windows and a contemplative interior. Museum admission includes Austin as well as the collection galleries and special exhibitions.
explore-bars.address: 200 East Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard, Austin, TX 78712
explore-bars.bestFor: Art lovers and a slower afternoon
explore-bars.tip: The later Saturday closing gives you more flexibility than the Bullock. Visit Austin in daylight to appreciate the colored glass.

explore-bars.name: Waterloo Park
explore-bars.kicker: Gardens and a Saturday morning celebration
explore-bars.description: A convenient green break near the Capitol, with landscaped paths, gathering spaces and the Moody Amphitheater. On this particular Saturday, the free Morning Glories Diwali celebration adds cultural performances, storytelling and hands-on activities. It is aimed especially at families with children, but makes a cheerful stop during a morning walk.
explore-bars.address: Waterloo Park, 1301 Trinity Street, Austin, TX 78701
explore-bars.hours: Park generally 5am–10pm; event access can vary. Diwali: Saturday Nov 7, 9am–noon
explore-bars.price: Park and Diwali program are free
explore-bars.tip: The Diwali activities take place at Meredith Heritage Tree Deck. Waterloo Greenway's new southern parkland is a separate option near the lake; the stretch between 4th and 12th Streets is still being developed.

sources.label: Waterloo Greenway: park hours and current sections

explore-bars.name: Central Library & Seaholm
explore-bars.kicker: A free view with a good lunch nearby
explore-bars.description: This is an excellent stop even if you are not looking for a book: explore the airy interior, then head to the roof garden for views toward downtown and Lady Bird Lake. The surrounding Seaholm and 2nd Street area makes it easy to combine the visit with lunch, a little browsing or dessert.
explore-bars.address: 710 West César Chávez Street, Austin, TX 78701
explore-bars.bestFor: Architecture, lake views and a relaxed afternoon
explore-bars.tip: Pair it with Local Foods or Flower Child for lunch, then The Baked Bear for dessert. The library connects to nearby trails if everyone wants a longer stroll.

sources.label: Austin Public Library: hours and location

explore-bars.name: Lady Bird Lake & the Butler Trail
explore-bars.kicker: Choose your own length of lake walk
explore-bars.description: Walk down Congress Avenue to the lake, then enjoy a manageable section of the waterfront trail. You can turn around whenever you like, or head west toward the library and pedestrian bridge. The complete trail is ten miles, so a short out-and-back is a better fit for a day with other plans.
explore-bars.address: Ann and Roy Butler Trail at Congress Avenue Bridge, Austin, TX 78701
explore-bars.hours: Plan this as a daylight outing
explore-bars.bestFor: A little exercise and skyline views
explore-bars.tip: Keep the walk west of Congress for an easy link with the library. If exploring farther east, check the trail's current detour map because work near I-35 affects parts of the boardwalk.

sources.label: The Trail Conservancy: visiting the Butler Trail
The Trail Conservancy: current construction and detours

explore-bars.name: South Congress browsing
explore-bars.kicker: Boots, murals and an unhurried wander
explore-bars.description: For a change from downtown, browse the shops and murals around South Congress. Think boots, gifts, coffee stops and people-watching rather than a single attraction with a ticket. Jo's Coffee and its familiar mural make a useful starting point, with the Continental Club nearby if you are continuing into an evening show.
explore-bars.address: Jo's Coffee, 1300 South Congress Avenue, Austin, TX 78704
explore-bars.hours: Best late morning or afternoon; individual shop hours vary
explore-bars.bestFor: Shopping, murals and a different neighborhood
explore-bars.tip: A ride one way keeps the outing easy. If walking, crossing Congress Avenue Bridge adds lake and skyline views along the way.

explore-bars.name: The Driskill Bar
explore-bars.kicker: An effortless first or last drink
explore-bars.description: The hotel's classic bar makes a comfortable choice for a pre-dinner cocktail or a final drink close to home. Reimagined alongside the Grill, it serves cocktails, beer and small plates around its distinctive hexagonal bar. This is a separate venue from The Victorian, the hotel's Western-style pub.
explore-bars.bestFor: Convenience and a classic hotel-bar setting
explore-bars.tip: A natural pairing with dinner at the Driskill Grill, or an easy meeting point before the group heads out.

sources.label: The Driskill Bar: menu, hours and setting

explore-bars.name: The Victorian
explore-bars.kicker: A Western pub at your own hotel
explore-bars.description: Old West saloon style meets an English-pub sensibility at this Driskill drinking spot, with cocktails, Texas-inspired pub food and a lively atmosphere. The mezzanine has billiards and card tables. It is a useful choice when everyone wants an enjoyable evening without adding another trip across town.
explore-bars.price: Cocktails and pub food à la carte
explore-bars.tip: The bar advertises live music Thursday–Saturday, 9pm–midnight. A named act for Nov 7 was not confirmed, so ask the concierge if music is your main reason for going.

sources.label: The Victorian: hours, menu and regular music schedule

explore-bars.name: The Roosevelt Room
explore-bars.description: A strong choice for a group that wants to sit down, order thoughtfully made drinks and let a knowledgeable staff guide the selection. The downstairs room offers table service and an extensive cocktail list. It works particularly well as a planned stop before dinner or a show, with a reservation to anchor the evening.
explore-bars.address: 307 West 5th Street, Unit B, Austin, TX 78701
explore-bars.bestFor: Cocktail enthusiasts and a polished group outing
explore-bars.tip: Walk-ins are welcome, but reservations are strongly recommended when you know your time. Read the booking terms when reserving.

sources.label: The Roosevelt Room: hours, service and reservations

explore-bars.name: Small Victory
explore-bars.description: A small, tucked-away room with blue banquettes, a discreet entrance and a serious interest in classic cocktails. Martinis, Manhattans and similar standards are the point here, with cheese and charcuterie for a light accompaniment. Its proximity to the hotel makes it especially appealing for an easy, intentional drink stop.
explore-bars.price: Cocktails and small bites; see current menu
explore-bars.bestFor: A martini and a small-room atmosphere
explore-bars.tip: Look carefully for the entrance by the parking garage and use the reservation link if the group has a fixed time.

sources.label: Small Victory: hours, address, menu and reservations

explore-bars.name: Firehouse Lounge
explore-bars.kicker: Through the bookshelf across the street
explore-bars.description: For a little novelty with almost no walking, cross Brazos and find the movable bookshelf in the Firehouse Hostel lobby. Behind it is a public cocktail lounge with local beers, zero-proof options and music on many nights. The playful entrance is part of the appeal; you do not need to be a hostel guest.
explore-bars.price: Happy hour: $6 margaritas, mules and martinis
explore-bars.tip: Enter the hostel at 605 Brazos and look for the bookshelf handle. Bring ID; the lounge is 21+. Check its calendar for any particular live performance.

sources.label: Firehouse Lounge: access, hours and happy hour

explore-bars.name: Casino El Camino
explore-bars.kicker: Burgers, dark corners and a great jukebox
explore-bars.description: A long-running rock-and-roll dive with a strong regulars tradition, a handpicked jukebox and substantial burgers. Its personality is a good fit for visitors seeking an unfussy local bar. The surrounding Sixth Street scene gets busier later, so an afternoon beer or early-evening visit is the most comfortable way to work it into this guide.
explore-bars.bestFor: A nearby dive with established local character
explore-bars.tip: Go earlier for a more relaxed visit. This is still Sixth Street, and the crowd on a particular Saturday can vary.

sources.label: Casino El Camino: hours and address
Visit Austin: neighborhood dive and burgers
Austin Monthly: Casino El Camino's regulars and jukebox

explore-bars.name: The Cloak Room
explore-bars.description: A dim, wood-paneled basement bar near the Capitol, known for its jukebox and connections to generations of political staff and regulars. This is the strongest nearby fit for an understated, old-Austin drink without a party-bar production. The room is small, so it is better for a compact group than a large gathering.
explore-bars.bestFor: A low-key dive with a Capitol crowd
explore-bars.tip: The entrance is down an outside stairwell. It opens late on Saturdays, so it will not work as a drink immediately after a daytime Capitol tour.

sources.label: Visit Austin: address and Saturday hours

explore-bars.name: Donn's Depot
explore-bars.kicker: A little farther for old-Austin dancing
explore-bars.description: A railway-depot bar with live music, two dance floors and a well-established mix of younger visitors and older regulars. It is a particularly appealing detour if the family wants a lived-in Austin institution with some movement to the evening. Think drinks and dancing; there is no full kitchen.
explore-bars.price: Saturday cover applies; amount varies by show
explore-bars.bestFor: A mixed-age local crowd and dancing
explore-bars.tip: Check the current music listing before making the ride. A specific Nov 7 act was not verified; this is a bar recommendation rather than a confirmed show listing.

sources.label: Donn's Depot: hours, age policy, cover and dancing
Visit Austin: Donn's history and mixed-age crowd

food.name: The Driskill Grill
food.description: A steakhouse evening without leaving the hotel: the historic dining room reopened in 2026 with dry-aged steaks, classic cocktails and substantial butcher’s cuts. Choose this for a relaxed special dinner when convenience matters as much as the food. The 10-layer chocolate cake makes an easy finish.
food.price: 8 oz tenderloin $72 · 16 oz Akaushi Wagyu ribeye $120 · sides extra
food.bestFor: A celebratory steak dinner with no travel
food.tip: Reserve a table. Dinner attire excludes shorts, flip-flops and slides.
details: Butcher’s cuts include bavette at $43 and tri-tip at $46, offering less expensive beef choices than the large steaks.
The 10-layer chocolate cake is $19; key lime pie is $15.

sources.label: Official restaurant, hours and dress code

food.name: Dean’s Italian Steakhouse
food.kicker: Steak for some, pasta for others
food.description: An Italian steakhouse close enough for an easy walk, with steaks alongside pasta and seafood. It works particularly well when some diners want a serious cut of beef and others would prefer a different main. Plan this as a sit-down dinner and reserve ahead for a Saturday table.
food.price: 10 oz flat iron $45 · 8 oz filet $66 · 22 oz dry-aged ribeye $110
food.bestFor: A steakhouse with good choices beyond beef
food.tip: A useful dinner pairing with nearby Congress Avenue music venues; allow time for a full restaurant meal.

food.name: Cooper’s Old Time Pit Bar-B-Que
food.description: The simplest downtown choice for a barbecue lunch or dinner, just down Congress Avenue from the hotel. Order meat and sides in a casual setting, then keep the rest of the day flexible. It is a particularly convenient option before nearby music or a walk along the lake.
food.price: Meat and sides priced separately; check current counter prices
food.tip: For a fixed-time show, leave a little room in the plan for ordering and any queue.
details: The menu includes several beef options, turkey and traditional sides. Current prices were not reliably posted on the official menu when checked.

food.name: Terry Black’s Barbecue
food.kicker: Brisket and beef ribs worth a detour
food.description: Make this the barbecue outing if brisket and a substantial beef rib are the main event. The location south of the river also pairs well with a Lady Bird Lake walk. Service is first come, first served, so leave room for a line and avoid a tightly timed show immediately afterward.
food.tip: Aim for an early lunch and keep the timing flexible. Ordinary dining is first come, first served.
details: Half a pound of brisket and two individual sides comes to about $29 before tax and drinks; this is a calculation, not a set combo.
Banana, peach and chocolate pudding are $4.75 each.

food.name: Roaring Fork
food.kicker: An easy dinner for a mixed group
food.description: A very short walk brings you to a broad Southwestern menu with steaks, a substantial burger, fish and chicken. This is an easy compromise for a group with different appetites, especially when a full steakhouse feels too formal. An early dinner also leaves time for a Saturday show.
food.hours: Saturday dinner: 4–10 pm · happy hour 4–6 pm in the bar and lounge
food.bestFor: A convenient dinner with something for everyone
food.tip: There is no Saturday lunch service. Happy-hour pricing applies in the bar and lounge only.
details: The 22 oz ribeye is listed at $64. The burger is $17 during happy hour.

sources.label: Official downtown menu, hours and reservations

food.name: Moonshine Patio Bar & Grill
food.kicker: Comfort food with an Austin feel
food.description: A useful all-rounder for Southern comfort food, with a Saturday brunch menu followed by regular lunch and dinner choices. Chicken-fried steak, steak frites and salmon give the table a good range, while hearty desserts suit anyone saving room for something sweet. The Red River location is an easy walk.
food.hours: Saturday: 10 am–10 pm · à la carte brunch 10 am–2 pm
food.price: Regular menu: chicken-fried steak $25 · salmon $28 · hanger steak frites $36
food.bestFor: Comfort food, brunch or a casual dinner
food.tip: Reservations are available through the restaurant’s website. The prices here are from the regular menu, not the brunch menu.
details: Bread pudding, banana cream pudding and peanut butter mousse pie are listed at $12 each.

food.name: La Condesa
food.description: A lively modern Mexican option near the Second Street shops, convenient for combining a meal with the library and downtown exploring. Saturday brunch offers both substantial beef dishes and smaller vegetable or salad choices. Dinner is another good occasion to make a reservation and settle in over a longer meal.
food.hours: Saturday brunch: 11 am–2 pm · dinner: 5–10 pm
food.price: Brunch: short-rib hash $22 · beef-cheek barbacoa $32 · chicken salad $19
food.bestFor: A Mexican brunch or a more leisurely dinner
food.tip: There is a break between brunch and dinner. These sample prices are specifically from the brunch menu.
details: A cauliflower tostada is listed at $18 on the brunch menu.

food.name: Salty Sow
food.description: Take a short ride to Manor Road for a dinner built around satisfying plates and a strong bar menu. Duck-fat fries, crispy chicken thighs and ribeye steak frites make this an appealing change of scene after a downtown day. It is best treated as a destination dinner rather than a quick walking stop.
food.price: Check the current menu for dish and happy-hour prices
food.bestFor: A dinner outing in a different neighborhood
food.tip: Reserve for Saturday and allow for the ride if you have a show afterward.

food.name: Local Foods
food.description: A particularly useful lunch stop around Second Street, with salads and grain bowls for lighter appetites and substantial sandwiches for everyone else. Sandwiches come with two market sides or a cup of soup. Pair it with the Central Library, Seaholm or the lake trail for an easy afternoon on foot.
food.hours: Saturday: 9 am–9 pm · all-day menu from 10:45 am · brunch until 3 pm
food.price: Green salad $15.50 · chicken farro bowl $19.50 · crunchy chicken sandwich $18
food.bestFor: A fresh lunch that still satisfies a bigger appetite
food.tip: The $22.50 Borracho Beef sandwich is a useful choice for a beef lover joining a lighter lunch.
details: The salmon poke bowl is listed at $21. Sandwich prices include two market sides or a cup of soup.

sources.label: Official Second Street location, hours and menu

food.name: Flower Child
food.description: This convenient downtown branch of a national chain is a good choice when you want vegetables, a salad or a protein plate without a long restaurant meal. Salmon, steak and tofu plates make it easy for different appetites to share a stop. The location pairs naturally with the library and Second Street.
food.bestFor: A lighter meal between larger dinners
food.tip: A protein plate with two vegetable sides is a useful way to keep the meal lighter and still substantial.
details: The vegetable salad is $11.25, with chicken available for an additional $6.25.

food.name: 1886 Café & Bakery
food.kicker: Lunch and cake without leaving the hotel
food.description: The hotel’s daytime café is an easy fallback when everyone wants a different pace. Greens and grain salads offer lighter lunches, while a burger or steak and eggs suits a bigger appetite. The bakery also makes a convenient afternoon treat, provided you get there before its early closing time.
food.price: Green salad $14 · grain salad $16 · burger $26 · chocolate cake $11
food.bestFor: An easy lunch or daytime dessert at the hotel
food.tip: Plan this for lunch, coffee or an afternoon cake stop; the café closes at 3 pm.
details: Grilled chicken can be added to a salad for $6.
Lemon tart is $11, hummingbird cake $9 and a chocolate-pecan croissant $7.

food.name: Voodoo Doughnut
food.description: A few minutes from the hotel, this colorful doughnut shop works for a quick treat or something to take back to the room. Expect playful toppings and oversized choices alongside simpler doughnuts. Its late hours are useful after a show, although Sixth Street itself becomes much busier later in the evening.
food.price: Plain glazed $1.75 · Portland Cream $4.25 · Bacon Maple Bar or Voodoo Doll $5
food.bestFor: Dessert very close to the hotel after a show
food.tip: The shop’s posted closing time is 3 am; online ordering can stop earlier.

food.name: Amy’s Ice Creams — West Sixth
food.description: Choose Amy’s when the dessert stop should feel like part of Austin rather than just the nearest sweet shop. Mexican Vanilla is the signature starting point, with mix-ins for anyone who wants something more elaborate. The West Sixth location is a longer but manageable downtown walk, or an easy stop during western downtown exploring.
food.price: Milkshake $7.50 on the posted pickup menu; scoop prices vary
food.bestFor: A local ice-cream stop while exploring west of Congress
food.tip: Use the West Sixth address here; Amy’s has several Austin locations.

sources.label: Official West Sixth location and hours
Official linked West Sixth pickup menu

food.name: The Baked Bear
food.description: Build an ice-cream sandwich with cookies or brownies at this Seaholm dessert shop. It is a particularly convenient reward after the Central Library or a lake walk, and the later opening hours also suit an evening stop. The portions make this a more substantial dessert than a quick bite of something sweet.
